mainEntity.name: Can I drink coffee immediately after dental bonding treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is generally advisable to avoid coffee for at least 48 hours after dental bonding. Composite resin is somewhat more porous in the initial post-treatment period, and the strong pigments in coffee can penetrate the surface and cause discolouration. Once the resin has fully matured, the staining risk reduces slightly, though regular coffee consumption can still gradually affect the colour of bonding over time. If you do drink coffee, rinsing with plain water immediately afterwards can help reduce the impact.

mainEntity.name: How long does dental bonding last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lifespan of dental bonding varies depending on the location of the bonding, your bite, your oral habits, and how well the treated area is maintained. With good care and regular dental reviews, composite bonding can last anywhere from three to ten years before any repair or refreshing may be needed. Your dentist is best placed to give you realistic expectations based on your specific clinical situation during a consultation.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal to feel sensitivity after dental bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mild sensitivity to hot and cold temperatures in the day or two following dental bonding is not unusual, particularly if the tooth required any preparation before the resin was applied. This typically settles within a few days. If sensitivity is significant, worsening, or does not resolve within a week or so, it is sensible to contact your dental team for a review, as this may occasionally indicate that further assessment is needed.

mainEntity.name: Can I use whitening toothpaste on bonded teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Highly abrasive whitening toothpastes are generally not recommended for use on composite-bonded teeth, as they can gradually dull the polished surface of the resin. It is worth noting that composite resin does not respond to tooth whitening agents in the same way that natural enamel does — so if you are considering teeth whitening alongside dental bonding, it is important to discuss the timing and sequencing with your dentist before treatment begins.

mainEntity.name: What foods should I completely avoid after dental bonding?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the immediate 24 to 48 hours following dental bonding, it is best to avoid hard, crunchy, or sticky foods — including crusty bread, raw vegetables, toffees, chewing gum, and nuts. Deeply pigmented foods such as beetroot, berries, curry, and tomato-based sauces should also be limited during this initial period due to their staining potential. After 48 hours, a normal diet can usually be resumed, though long-term mindfulness about very hard foods and staining substances is worthwhile.

mainEntity.name: Does dental bonding require any special aftercare products?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, no specialist products are required following dental bonding. A soft-bristled toothbrush, a gentle low-abrasive fluoride toothpaste, and an alcohol-free mouthwash are generally all that is needed for day-to-day care. Your dental team may have specific recommendations based on your individual treatment, so it is always worth asking before you leave your appointment if you are unsure about any products.
